id_note: Rule IDs (GDS-*) are local to this library, not official GOV.UK identifiers. rule_paraphrase is our own wording, not quotation.

rules.rule_paraphrase: When validation fails, show an error summary at the top of the page as well as an inline error message beside each answer with an error; show the summary even when there is only one error.
rules.heading: When to use this component

rules.rule_paraphrase: The error summary uses the heading 'There is a problem'.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: Each entry in the error summary links to the answer it relates to: the field itself for single-field questions; the first field in error for multi-field questions such as date input (or the first field if unknown); the first radio or checkbox for option lists.
rules.heading: Linking from the error summary to each answer

rules.rule_paraphrase: Place the error summary at the top of the main container, below any breadcrumbs or back link and above the h1.
rules.heading: Where to put the error summary

rules.rule_paraphrase: Move keyboard focus to the error summary when it is shown (govuk-frontend JavaScript does this).
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: Error text in the summary must be worded identically to the inline message next to the field.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: On a page re-shown after failed validation, prefix the document <title> with 'Error: '.
rules.heading: How to tell the user about validation errors

rules.rule_paraphrase: Re-show the page with the user's answers as entered; do not clear either passing or failing fields.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: Inline error messages sit after the question and hint text and include a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix for screen reader users (the prefix may be translated).
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: Error messages reuse wording from the question label or legend so the message can be matched to the field.
rules.heading: Match up error messages to labels

rules.rule_paraphrase: Error wording avoids technical jargon, blame words such as 'forbidden', 'illegal' or 'you forgot', and the words 'please', 'sorry', 'valid'/'invalid' and informal terms like 'oops'.
rules.heading: Be clear and concise

rules.rule_paraphrase: Avoid generic errors such as 'An error occurred' or 'This field is required'; give a specific message per error state (empty, too long, too short, disallowed characters, wrong format).
rules.heading: Be specific

rules.rule_paraphrase: Do not use error messages for eligibility, permission or service-capacity problems; send the user to a page explaining the problem and next steps.
rules.heading: When not to use this component

rules.rule_paraphrase: Empty text input error follows the template 'Enter [whatever it is]'; other states (length, numbers, money) have their own templates.
rules.heading: Error messages

rules.rule_paraphrase: Radios errors: yes/no questions use 'Select yes if ...'; two non-yes/no options use 'Select if ...'; more than two options use 'Select [whatever it is]'.
rules.heading: Error messages

rules.rule_paraphrase: Date input: when several errors apply show only the highest priority (missing/incomplete, then impossible values, then other validation failures); highlight only the field(s) at fault, or the whole date where the guidance says so.
rules.heading: Error messages

rules.rule_paraphrase: Turn off browser HTML5 validation by adding novalidate to the form, and do not put the required attribute on inputs.
rules.heading: Turn off HTML5 validation

rules.rule_paraphrase: Always validate server side, even when client side validation is also used.
rules.heading: Client side and server side validation

rules.rule_paraphrase: Do not validate when the user leaves a field; validate when they try to continue or submit, unless research supports live validation.
rules.heading: When to tell the user about validation errors

rules.rule_paraphrase: Ignore unwanted characters (spaces, hyphens, brackets, punctuation, leading/trailing characters) in numbers and codes rather than raising an error, unless it makes the data unusable.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: Start with one question per page; where a page has a single question, the label or legend can be set as the page heading.
rules.heading: Start by asking one question per page

rules.rule_paraphrase: Question pages include a back link, a page heading and a continue button.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: Never mark mandatory fields with asterisks; mark optional fields with '(optional)' in the label (or legend for radios/checkboxes).
rules.heading: When to use this pattern

rules.rule_paraphrase: Hint text is one short sentence without full stops and contains no links.
rules.heading: Hint text

rules.rule_paraphrase: The continue button reads 'Continue' (not 'Next') and is left-aligned.
rules.heading: Continue button

rules.rule_paraphrase: Do not reuse the same page heading across multiple pages.
rules.heading: Page headings

rules.rule_paraphrase: Do not break the browser back button; it should return users to the previous page in the state they left it.
rules.heading: Back link

rules.rule_paraphrase: Avoid range sliders; if one is used, provide a way to answer without click-and-drag (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.1).
rules.heading: Using range sliders

rules.rule_paraphrase: Every text input has a label, normally visible, placed above the input, in sentence case without a trailing colon.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: Do not use placeholder text as a label, hint or example.
rules.heading: Avoid placeholder text

rules.rule_paraphrase: For whole numbers use inputmode='numeric' (or 'decimal' for decimals); avoid input type='number' unless research shows a need.
rules.heading: Numbers

rules.rule_paraphrase: Do not block copy and paste into text inputs.
rules.heading: Do not disable copy and paste

rules.rule_paraphrase: Avoid the maxlength attribute; if a limit is needed, state it in the hint and only error on values that are still too long after normalisation.
rules.heading: Avoid restricting the length of a user's input

rules.rule_paraphrase: Set spellcheck='false' on inputs where spellcheck is inappropriate, such as names, email addresses and reference numbers.
rules.heading: How and when to spellcheck a user’s input

rules.rule_paraphrase: Prefixes/suffixes must not be the only indication of required units; say it in the label or hint too, because screen readers do not announce them.
rules.heading: Prefixes and suffixes

rules.rule_paraphrase: In production, set an autocomplete attribute on inputs that collect user data with a WCAG input purpose (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.5, level AA).
rules.heading: Use the autocomplete attribute

rules.rule_paraphrase: Name fields: autocomplete='name' for a single full-name field; 'given-name' and 'family-name' for split fields.
rules.heading: Use the autocomplete attribute on name fields

rules.rule_paraphrase: Email fields use type='email', autocomplete='email', spellcheck='false', allow pasting, and accept up to 254 characters.
rules.heading: Help users to enter a valid email address

rules.rule_paraphrase: Phone number inputs use autocomplete='tel' and accept spaces, hyphens, brackets and country/area codes.
rules.heading: Use the autocomplete attribute

rules.rule_paraphrase: Date of birth inputs set autocomplete to bday-day, bday-month and bday-year on the three fields.
rules.heading: Use the autocomplete attribute for a date of birth

rules.rule_paraphrase: Address fields: each separate field gets its matching input purpose; a single textarea address uses autocomplete='street-address'.
rules.heading: Use the autocomplete attribute on multiple address fields

rules.rule_paraphrase: Middle names field is optional and its label does not include '(optional)'; avoid asking for title, and if you must, use an optional text input not a select.
rules.heading: Middle names

rules.rule_paraphrase: Accept postcodes in any case, with or without spaces, and with stray punctuation; make county optional.
rules.heading: Allow different postcode formats

rules.rule_paraphrase: Avoid input masking and do not reformat phone numbers shown back to users.
rules.heading: Avoid input masking

rules.rule_paraphrase: Group radios and checkboxes in a fieldset with a legend describing them; the legend is the first element inside the fieldset.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: Do not pre-select radio or checkbox options; place controls to the left of labels.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: Conditionally reveal only simple questions (never non-question content) and never from inline radios.
rules.heading: Conditionally revealing a related question

rules.rule_paraphrase: Where 'none' is valid for checkboxes, add a 'none' option last, separated by an 'or' divider, with a label repeating the question.
rules.heading: Add an option for ‘none’

rules.rule_paraphrase: Date input is three fields (day, month, year) in a fieldset; never auto-advance focus between fields; accept month names.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: A JavaScript calendar picker must never be the only way to enter a date; also allow text entry.
rules.heading: Helping users to pick a date

rules.rule_paraphrase: Button text is sentence case and describes the action; primary button aligned left; avoid multiple default (primary) buttons on a page.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: Avoid disabled buttons unless research shows they make the interface easier to understand.
rules.heading: Disabled buttons

rules.rule_paraphrase: Start buttons use a link element rather than a button element, since they do not submit data.
rules.heading: Start buttons

rules.rule_paraphrase: Warning buttons are reserved for serious irreversible actions, ideally after a confirmation step, and must not rely on red colour alone.
rules.heading: Warning buttons

rules.rule_paraphrase: Check answers page: 'Change' link per item with visually hidden text describing what it changes; skipped optional answers shown as 'Not provided'; submit button text describes the action.
rules.heading: Let users go back and change their answers

rules.rule_paraphrase: After changing an answer, 'Continue' returns the user to the check answers page with answers pre-populated.
rules.heading: Let users go back and change their answers

rules.rule_paraphrase: Confirmation page includes reference number (if any), what happens next, service contact details, likely next links, a feedback link and a way to save a record.
rules.heading: How it works

rules.rule_paraphrase: A service start point explains what the service does, has a start button whose text matches the action, lists cost/time and other ways to access the service, and avoids complex eligibility rules.
rules.heading: How it works
